questions.question: Why does the USPSTF I statement on routine skin-cancer screening not apply to a changing mole?
choices: A changing lesion is a diagnostic evaluation problem, not an asymptomatic screening scenario
The I statement proves every mole is benign
Only dermatologists can examine skin
Skin screening and lesion evaluation are identical
questions.explanation: USPSTF screening guidance applies to asymptomatic people; changing, irregular, or symptomatic lesions need diagnostic assessment.

questions.question: Which melanoma feature is represented by the E in ABCDE?
choices: Evolving change in a lesion
Excess moisturizer
Exercise intolerance
Erythema only
questions.explanation: Evolving size, shape, color, surface, or symptoms is an important melanoma clue, even when other features are absent.

questions.question: What is the ugly-duckling sign?
choices: A lesion that looks different from the patient’s other lesions
A mole that is always larger than 6 mm
A lesion that never changes
A normal skin fold
questions.explanation: A lesion that differs from the patient’s usual pattern can be concerning and supports diagnostic assessment.

questions.question: Which nonpigmented lesion pattern warrants reassessment?
choices: A persistent bleeding, crusted, ulcerated, tender, or nonhealing lesion
A short-lived scratch that heals normally
Stable normal skin texture
Improved dryness with moisturizer
questions.explanation: Persistent nonhealing, bleeding, ulcerated, or changing lesions can represent keratinocyte cancer or another condition requiring assessment.

questions.question: What should be documented for a suspicious lesion?
choices: Exact site, size, morphology, color, border, surface, symptoms, duration, and evolution
Only the patient’s age
Only a diagnosis label
Nothing until pathology returns
questions.explanation: Precise documentation supports comparison, referral, and safe diagnostic follow-up.

questions.question: Why should a suspicious possible melanoma lesion not be casually destroyed with destructive treatment?
choices: Tissue diagnosis and appropriate biopsy technique may be needed for accurate histopathology and staging
Destructive treatment always cures melanoma
Pathology is unnecessary
Lesions should never be evaluated
questions.explanation: Appropriate biopsy preserves essential diagnostic and staging information when melanoma is possible.

questions.question: Which patient statement requires correction?
choices: People with darker skin cannot develop melanoma
A changing acral lesion needs assessment
Skin cancer can occur in all skin tones
A new nail pigment change may need evaluation
questions.explanation: Skin cancer occurs in all skin tones; dismissing a concerning acral, nail, or evolving lesion based on complexion is unsafe.

questions.question: What is a closed-loop responsibility after biopsy or dermatology referral?
choices: Confirm the pathology/referral result, notify the patient, and document treatment/surveillance ownership
Assume no news is good news
Delete the result after filing
Leave patient notification to chance
questions.explanation: Diagnostic safety requires documented result review, patient communication, and a plan for definitive follow-up.

questions.question: Which prevention message is most appropriate?
choices: Use practical UV protection and avoid indoor tanning while remaining alert for changing lesions
Sunscreen eliminates all skin-cancer risk
Only fair-skinned people need UV protection
Skin self-awareness is unnecessary
questions.explanation: UV protection and prompt attention to changing lesions are practical prevention/awareness strategies, but no measure eliminates all risk.

questions.question: What is the FNP-level suspicious lesion principle?
choices: Dismiss lesions when the patient has no family history
Integrate evolution, morphology, risk context, diagnostic pathway, and closed-loop follow-up
Use ABCDE as the only diagnostic test
Treat every lesion in the emergency department
questions.explanation: High-quality care distinguishes screening from diagnostic evaluation, preserves tissue when needed, and ensures referral/pathology follow-up.
